title: "I am first and I am last": the whole chain in short, and the Aibershter mamash here
overview: Chapter 7 begins the second part of the book: after the chapters on what *hisbonenus* is, a general overview of the *hishtalshelus* it is done on, so that every particular learned later fits into the *klal*. From *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum* to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* it is one chain, and the end is wedged in the beginning: "I am first and I am last." Above the chain is the Essence before the *tzimtzum*; below it are we and the physical world, and it is *davka* there, in the bunnies of *Tehillim*, that the *Ein Sof* rests. A King is king at His borders, and every unification is only a *prat* before what is above it. The middle is transparent, like a phone line, and in the *Kesarim* it is all one will. For Rabbi Markel the point is that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here, on the conference call. A last class talks freely about learning the book: *Shaar HaYichud* is a kindergarten book that shows you are a worm, and learning it takes *mesirus nefesh*, giving up the will to be a big shot.

sections.title: One chain from first to last: the point is that the Aibershter is mamash here
sections.summary: Chapter 7 opens the second part of the book with a general overview of the *hishtalshelus*, so that every particular learned later fits into the *klal*. From the first to the last it is one chain, "I am first and I am last", and the whole purpose of contemplating the particulars is to see that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here, standing and listening.

phrases.he: (ז) ומעתה יש להקדים בתחלה
phrases.en: (7) And now we must first set out,

phrases.he: וקודם להידיעה בפרטות כל ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: before the knowledge of the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) in its particulars,

phrases.he: ענין הנזכר לעיל (באות ד')
phrases.en: the matter mentioned above (in chapter 4):

phrases.he: בחיבור הפרט עם הכלל דווקא כו'
phrases.en: the joining of the *prat* (particular) with the *klal* (whole), *davka*.

blocks.text: With chapter 7 the second part of the book really begins. Up to now came the explanations of what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is, how to be *misbonen* and what to be *misbonen* on, and the various introductions, the *yesh* and the *ayin* "and all this business." Now comes the explanation of the actual *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) that the *hisbonenus* is supposed to be on. And even though he said that the whole thing is in the particulars, first he has to give the general overview. That is basically what chapter 7 is: a general overview.

**the joining of the *prat* (particular) with the *klal* (whole), *davka***. So first of all comes what the general overview is, so that later on, when all the particulars are given, you will know where each one fits into the *klal*.

phrases.he: בהיות ידוע לכל מעיין בספר הזוהר ובספרי הקבלה האמיתים
phrases.en: As is known to everyone who looks into the *Zohar* and the true books of Kabbala

phrases.he: בהשתלשלות והתלבשות הפרצופים כו'
phrases.en: about the descent and enclothing of the *partzufim* (configurations),

phrases.he: בסדר קצר ההכרחי לכל אדם לידע
phrases.en: in the short order that every person needs to know:

phrases.he: מתחלה אחדות הפשוטה מריש כל דרגין
phrases.en: first the simple unity, from the head of all levels

phrases.he: עד סוף כל דרגין בסוף עולם השפל שלנו
phrases.en: to the end of all levels, at the end of our lowly world,

phrases.he: שהוא בא בחיבור וקשר אחד ממש
phrases.en: which comes in one joining and bond, *mamash*,

phrases.he: מראש לסוף ממש כשלשלת כו'
phrases.en: from the beginning to the end, *mamash*, like a chain,

phrases.he: שמשתלשל מעילה לעילה כו'
phrases.en: that descends from cause to cause.

blocks.text: The *Zohar* and the true books of Kabbala describe the descent and enclothing of the *partzufim*; here is the short order of it that every person needs to know. From the simple unity at the head of all levels to the end of all levels, at the end of our lowly world, it **comes in one joining and bond, *mamash***. It is really all one connected thing, not a whole bunch of different things, from the beginning to the end, *mamash*, like a chain.

This is a very important thing, and a lot of people make mistakes on it: they actually think that the *sefiros* are things, separate things. As it says, *kol man d'afrish chad mechavrei*: whoever separates one of the ten *sefiros* from another, it is as if he made a blemish in the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). It is as if he separated the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: ואור הראשון דאחדות הפשוט שנקרא עילת כל העילת
phrases.en: And the first light of the simple unity, which is called the cause of all causes,

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא ראשון או קדמון
phrases.en: is what is called First or *Kadmon* (preceding),

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני ראשון ואני אחרון
phrases.en: as it is written, "I am first and I am last."

phrases.he: אני ראשון הוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף אחר הצמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: "I am first" is *Malchus* (kingship) of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite) after the first *tzimtzum* (contraction), which is called the *makom panui* (the empty place);

phrases.he: ואני אחרון סוף הכל הוא בחינת מלכות דמלכות דעשיה מקור התהוות זה העולם השפל
phrases.en: and "I am last," the end of everything, is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the source from which this lowly world comes into being.

phrases.he: ונעוץ תחלתן בסופן וסופן בתחלתן
phrases.en: Their beginning is wedged in their end and their end in their beginning,

phrases.he: והיו לאחדים ממש כשלשלת
phrases.en: and they become one, *mamash*, like a chain,

phrases.he: שהאחרונה ביותר קשורה בהעליונה ביותר
phrases.en: in which the very last is bound to the very highest.

blocks.text: The first light of the simple unity, the cause of all causes, is called First, as it says: **"I am first and I am last."** I'm the first, I'm the last. "I am first" is *Malchus* (kingship) of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite) after the first *tzimtzum* (contraction), the *makom panui* (the empty place); "I am last" is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* (the world of Action), the source of this lowly world. So it is all the same.

blocks.title: The chain and the necklace
blocks.text: **Their beginning is wedged in their end**, and they are one: not two different things, *mamash* one thing, **like a chain**, in which the last is bound to the highest. When you put a chain together, the end of the chain connects to the beginning. And it is *davka* the end of the chain that is more connected to the beginning than the middle links. (A student: "Like a necklace." "Like a necklace, right.") It is the end of the chain that gets connected to the beginning of the chain.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב ראו כי אני אני הוא,
phrases.en: And this is what is written, "See that I, I am He":

phrases.he: בלא שינוי מראש לסוף כלל
phrases.en: with no change at all from beginning to end.

blocks.text: **"See that I, I am He"**: you should see that the same One who is down here is the same One who is up there, **with no change at all from beginning to end**, *mamash* no change. That is the whole *inyan* (matter) of what you are supposed to get here. If it looks to you like two different things, you are not really getting it. That is not what *Chassidus* is all about. *Chassidus* means that all the way down to here is *mamash* the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: והגם שידוע שיש ריבוי פרטי השתלשלות מאד מאד מראש לסוף,
phrases.en: And even though it is known that there are very, very many particulars of the *hishtalshelus* from beginning to end,

phrases.he: הנה זה כל האדם
phrases.en: this is the whole of man:

phrases.he: בהתבוננות כל פרטי פרטיות מראש לסוף,
phrases.en: in the contemplation of all the particulars of particulars from beginning to end,

phrases.he: לחבר הכל ליחוד הכללי דאחדות הפשוט הנקרא ראשון
phrases.en: to join everything to the general unification of the simple unity, which is called First.

blocks.text: There are really very, very many particular things in the *hishtalshelus* from beginning to end, but **this is the whole of man**: this is the whole reason you are here, your whole purpose in the world. The whole reason you have to do the *hisbonenus* of all the particulars is to connect the whole thing to the simple unity at the beginning of the whole thing. It means that the whole thing is a matter of *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him).

So if you are learning this like those people who learn Kabbala and want to know how to meditate on the *sefiros*, or to know which *sefira* is acting, "this is total baloney." It is not what it is all about. The whole *inyan* is that the *Aibershter* is here, *mamash* here, standing.

blocks.text: This is one of the Rebbe's twelve *pesukim*: "And behold, G-d stands over him, and the whole earth is full of His glory; and He looks upon him and searches his kidneys and heart, whether he serves Him as is fitting." That is the whole *inyan* of *Chassidus*: the *Aibershter* is *mamash* standing here looking at us, to see if we are worshipping Him properly, one hundred percent. And we just talked about how to do one hundred percent. There is only one way to do one hundred percent: with *hisbonenus*.

blocks.title: The Aibershter on the conference call
blocks.text:
The whole *inyan* of the *hisbonenus* is not to figure out which *sefira*, or where to make your *kavanos* (intentions), "or nothing like that." No. It means the *Aibershter* is *mamash* standing here. Right now Shimon made a conference call, and it was made to the *Aibershter* also: the *Aibershter* is also listening in on us. He is looking at us and listening very closely, to see if we are learning this properly, learning the *Aibershter*, or learning it for a self-serving motive. It is very important to Him, and He is totally involved in this thing.

And He checks not only by listening: He can look inside our *kishkes* (guts). ("*Bochen klayos*." "*Bochen klayos valev*.") He can look inside our kidneys and our hearts to see why we are learning this. Are we really trying to catch the essential *tevuna*, or do we want to cash in on it somehow? Is there a self-serving motive in here? That is the whole *inyan*: you have to connect the whole end of it, right down here where we are, all the way up to the simple unity.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני אני הוא ממש
phrases.en: As it is written, "I, I am He," *mamash*,

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'
phrases.en: and as it is written, "I, *Havaya*, have not changed."

blocks.text: **"I, I am He," *mamash***: the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here. In other words, the same way that I am here and the same way that you are here, the same way the *Aibershter* is here on the conference call, *mamash* like that. (A student: "Even more so." "Even more so, right.")

blocks.title: "I'm with you in spirit"
blocks.text: It is not like when somebody cannot make it to a wedding and says, "I'm with you in spirit." "Yeah, you're with me in spirit, but you're not really here. So at least send your check; it should be here in physicality." "Oh, the check is also there in spirit." No, it is not in spirit. The *Aibershter* is not here in spirit. He is *mamash* here, just like a physical, actual thing. He is listening; He can hear every word we are saying.

**"I, *Havaya*, have not changed."** Even though He is called First, it is *mamash* the same *Aibershter* down here. It is not that this is a *tzimtzum* of the *Aibershter* down here. It is *mamash* His very Essence and being, *atzmuso umahuso*, that is on the conference call with us.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר קוטב היסוד המוסד בהתבוננות הפרט דוקא,
phrases.en: And this is the main pivot of the foundation laid in the contemplation of the particular, *davka*:

phrases.he: שיומשך הכל אל הכלל כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: that everything be drawn to the *klal*, as mentioned above.

blocks.text: This is **the main pivot of the foundation** laid in the contemplation of the particular: **that everything be drawn to the *klal***. So the whole thing is that *mamash* the *Aibershter* is here.

sections.title: The short order: from He and His Name down to Malchus of Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: Before the *tzimtzum* there was He and His light, filling a *chalal* that nobody asks about. Then came the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav*, and the chain in which each world's *Malchus* becomes the *Keser* of the next, down to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the end of G-dliness.

phrases.he: וביאור הדבר למתחילים,
phrases.en: To explain this for beginners:

phrases.he: הנה ידוע בדרך קצרה
phrases.en: it is known, in a short way,

phrases.he: בסדר ריבוי השתלשלות דבחינת הקו וחוט שנמשך אחר צמצום הראשון,
phrases.en: the order of the many steps of the descent of the *Kav* (line) and thread that is drawn after the first *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: הוא כך
phrases.en: This is how it is.

phrases.he: דבתחלה קודם הצמצום הראשון היה הוא ושמו בלבד כו'
phrases.en: At first, before the first *tzimtzum*, there was He and His Name alone:

phrases.he: דהיינו עצמיות אין סוף ברוך הוא ואורו וזיוו הנקרא שמו
phrases.en: that is, the Essence of the *Ein Sof*, blessed be He, and His light and radiance, which is called His Name.

phrases.he: הכל היה בבחינת עצמיות שלו בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: Everything was in His own essence, as *Ein Sof*, *mamash*,

phrases.he: והיה ממלא את כל החלל כו'
phrases.en: and it filled the whole *chalal* (space).

blocks.text: **To explain this for beginners**, he now gives the short overview: the order of the *Kav* (line) and thread that is drawn after the first *tzimtzum*. "This is how it is." **At first, before the first *tzimtzum*, there was He and His Name alone**: just Him and the light. There was the Essence of the *Ein Sof* and the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), which is called His Name. Everything was in His own essence, as *Ein Sof*, *mamash*.

blocks.question: "And it filled the whole chalal": what chalal? There was nothing but the Aibershter, so where did this space come from?
blocks.text: "It's a funny thing, nobody ever asked a question over here." It says that the *Ein Sof* and His light filled up the whole *chalal* (space). What *chalal*? Rabbi Markel learned this with many, many people; you say this thing and they ask all kinds of questions, but nobody ever thinks, what *chalal*?, because to them space is a pre-existing thing: there is a space. So it seems to him, *b'derech efshar* (as a possibility), that the *chalal* is actually an even higher level than the *Atzmus* (the Essence), because the *Atzmus* and the light apparently need a place to be in. He was filling the whole *chalal*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך צמצם את עצמו
phrases.en: Then He contracted Himself,

phrases.he: ונשאר בחינת רשימו מן הצמצום שבחלל זה
phrases.en: and there remained a *reshimu* (an impression) of the *tzimtzum* in this *chalal*.

phrases.he: ומרושם זה נמשך בחינת הקו וחוט בבחינת מקיף ופנימי כו'
phrases.en: From this impression the *Kav* and thread is drawn, as *makif* (encompassing) and *pnimi* (inner).

phrases.he: ונקרא אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום בשם טהירו עילאה
phrases.en: The *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* is called *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity),

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף הכללי דקו זה בראשיתו נקרא טהירו תתאה כידוע
phrases.en: and the general *makif* of this *Kav*, at its beginning, is called *tehiru tata'a* (the lower purity), as is known.

blocks.text: **Then He contracted Himself**, and there remained a *reshimu* (impression) of the *tzimtzum* in this *chalal*. From that impression the *Kav* and thread is drawn, as *makif* (encompassing light) and *pnimi* (inner light). The light before the *tzimtzum* is called *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), and the general *makif* of the *Kav* at its beginning is the *tehiru tata'a* (the lower purity). So now he is basically going over the whole general *inyan* of the *hishtalshelus*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך נמשך על ידי צמצום, מלכות דאין סוף להיות כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: Then, through a *tzimtzum*, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* is drawn down to become *Keser* (crown) of *Adam Kadmon*;

phrases.he: וממלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר לעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין
phrases.en: from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes *Keser* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*;

phrases.he: וממלכות דאריך אנפין נעשה כתר לאבא ואמא
phrases.en: from *Malchus* of *Arich Anpin* comes *Keser* of *Abba* and *Ima*;

phrases.he: וממלכות דאבא ואמא נעשה כתר לזעיר אנפין ומזעיר אנפין לנוקבא
phrases.en: from *Malchus* of *Abba* and *Ima*, *Keser* of *Zeir Anpin*, and from *Zeir Anpin* to *Nukva*;

phrases.he: עד שממלכות דאצילות נעשה כתר לבריאה
phrases.en: until *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*.

phrases.he: וכך מבריאה ליצירה ומיצירה לעשיה
phrases.en: And so from *Beriya* to *Yetzira*, and from *Yetzira* to *Asiya*,

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות שבמלכות דעשיה סוף הכל כו'
phrases.en: down to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the end of everything.

blocks.text: Then *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* is drawn down through a *tzimtzum* to become *Keser* (crown) of *Adam Kadmon*; *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes *Keser* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, and so on through *Abba*, *Ima*, *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, **until *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya***. "That's how it works." Then the whole thing goes over again in *Beriya*: all these levels go over again in *Beriya* till *Malchus* of *Beriya* becomes *Keser* of *Yetzira*, and then again from *Yetzira* to *Asiya*.

blocks.question: "Down to Malchus of Malchus of Asiya, the end of everything": what do you mean, the end of everything? Where are we? Where do we fit in?
blocks.text: This keeps going all the way down to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, **the end of everything**. Where do we fit in? Well, he did not get to us yet. "The end of everything" means the end of *Elokus* (G-dliness). After it comes the actual world of the *kelipos* (husks).

sections.title: The end wedged in the beginning, and the two levels left out
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is wedged in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: "I am first and I am last." The Essence before the *tzimtzum* is above beginning and end, and we are below the chain; and it is we who connect to the Essence, through the mitzvos.

phrases.he: ונמצא סוף הכל שהוא מלכות דמלכות דעשיה,
phrases.en: So the end of everything, *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: נעוץ בתחלת הכל שהוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שמתצמצם להיות כתר לאדם קדמון
phrases.en: is wedged in the beginning of everything, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* that contracts to become *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בהתחלתו בשער הכללים,
phrases.en: as is explained in *Etz Chaim*, at its beginning, in *Shaar HaKlalim*.

phrases.he: והיינו אני ראשון ואני אחרון כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And this is "I am first and I am last," as mentioned above.

blocks.text: **So the end of everything**, *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, is wedged in the beginning of everything, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* as it contracts to become *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, as *Etz Chaim* explains at its very beginning. And this is what "I am first and I am last" means: "I am first" is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, and "I am last" is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן בחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: (But the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: לא נקרא עדיין גם בשם תחלה וסוף
phrases.en: is not yet called even by the name of beginning and end,

phrases.he: כי הרי הוא בחינת אור עצמות עדיין כמו שהוא טרם שנמשך בשביל השפעה למטה
phrases.en: for it is still the light of the Essence as it is, before it was drawn out to give forth below,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אתה קדוש ושמך קדוש כו' כידוע)
phrases.en: as it is written, "You are holy and Your Name is holy," as is known.)

blocks.text: But the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* **is not yet called even by the name of beginning and end**: it is still the light of the Essence as it is, before it was drawn out to give forth below. Notice that he says this whole *hishtalshelus* runs from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum* to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. So it seems there are two levels he is leaving out of it: the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, which is higher than the *hishtalshelus*, and us, who are lower than the *hishtalshelus*.

And that is the thing: really we are the ones who connect to the actual *Atzmus*, through the mitzvos "and stuff like that." As it says, "**You are holy and Your Name is holy**": both You, Himself, and the light are holy, totally removed. They have nothing to do with all this *hishtalshelus*.

sections.title: The two unifications of the Shema, and a King is made at the borders
sections.summary: Contemplating every particular from top to bottom draws it all up to the Essence before the *tzimtzum*: that is "*Havaya* is One", the *yichuda ila'a*. "Blessed be the Name" is the *yichuda tata'a*, one *Malchus* down to *Asiya*; and since a king is king at his borders, *Malchus* of *Asiya* is the biggest *Malchus*, and we push the border out by conquering the world for Him.

phrases.he: והנה אחר, היחוד
phrases.en: But the unification:

phrases.he: בהתבוננות היטב בכל פרטי ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: only with a good contemplation of all the particulars of the *hishtalshelus*,

phrases.he: מריש כל דרגין שהוא מלכות דאין סוף עד מלכות דעשיה דוקא,
phrases.en: from the head of all levels, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, *davka*:

phrases.he: אזי יומשך הכל אל המקור הראשון
phrases.en: then everything will be drawn to the first source,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: The text now explains **the unification**. Only when you look well and understand all the particulars, **from the head of all levels, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, *davka***, from the beginning to the end, then **everything will be drawn to the first source**. Only then can you pull the whole thing even higher than *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*. To what? To the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והיינו כוונה כללית דפסוק ראשון ביחודא עילאה דקריאת שמע
phrases.en: And this is the general *kavana* (intention) of the first verse, the *yichuda ila'a* (upper unification) of the *Shema*:

phrases.he: יהו״ה אחד,
phrases.en: "*Havaya* is One":

phrases.he: אחדות פשוט ממש שלפני הצמצום הראשון,
phrases.en: a simple unity, *mamash*, before the first *tzimtzum*;

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר בספר יצירה לפני אחד מה אתה סופר
phrases.en: of which the *Sefer Yetzira* says, "Before one, what do you count?"

phrases.he: למעלה מי׳ ספירות כו'
phrases.en: above the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: וכמאמר אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י׳ ספירות כו' וכידוע
phrases.en: And as the saying goes, "You are One, and not in the count of the ten *sefiros*," as is known.

blocks.text: This is the general *kavana* (intention) of the first verse of the *Shema*, the *yichuda ila'a* (the upper unification): **"*Havaya* is One"**, a simple unity, *mamash*, before the first *tzimtzum*. That is the *kavana* of *Shema Yisroel*. Of this the *Sefer Yetzira* says, "Before one, what do you count?" Higher than the ten *sefiros* of *Echad*, what do you count? In fact it explains in various places that "*Havaya* is One" really refers to *Yachid* (the Singular), and to how *Echad* is included in *Yachid*. As the saying goes, "You are One, and not in the count of the ten *sefiros*": not even in a count of ten *sefiros*, a totally higher level, as will be explained later in chapter 10.

phrases.he: וכוונה כללית דברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד ביחודא תתאה
phrases.en: And the general *kavana* of "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever," the *yichuda tata'a* (lower unification),

phrases.he: הוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים,
phrases.en: of which it says, "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds,"

phrases.he: עד מלכות דעשיה שהוא ענין אני ראשון ואני אחרון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*; which is the matter of "I am first and I am last" mentioned above.

blocks.text: The general *kavana* of "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever," the *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unification), is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*. Of this it says, **"Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds,"** from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum* down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. It is the same *Malchus*. That is the way of a king's *Malchus*: it is the same *Malchus* from Hodu to Kush. And that is what "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His kingdom, *l'olam va'ed*" means; and *va'ed* is *echad*.

"Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds" means that it is not a different *Malchus*: as if *Malchus* of *Atzilus* were a great *Malchus*, and *Malchus* of *Beriya* a lower one because it is a contracted *Malchus*, and so on all the way down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. It is *mamash* the same *Malchus*. Not only that: really *Malchus* of *Asiya* is a bigger *Malchus* than *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, because in *Malchus* the external is more important than the internal.

blocks.title: The palace and the borders
blocks.text: The biggest *Malchus* is not at the palace, it is at the border. That is what makes the king's *Malchus*: *davka* the border. If he wants to become a bigger king, he does not do it by making his palace bigger; he makes himself a bigger king by making his borders bigger, by pushing out the borders. That is why it says that Achashverosh was the king from Hodu till Kush. It does not talk about Shushan the capital. ("Hodu and Kush are the extremities." "The extremities.") It is from here till there. Over here, for instance, we would say America is from Canada till Mexico. What does it have to do with Canada and Mexico? Why don't we say the middle of Washington, which is where the *Malchus* is? No. When you describe the *Malchus*, it is from one end to the other end, from the faraway corners, not from the inside of the palace. The thing of the *Malchus* is *davka* the borders.

So the biggest *Malchus* is *davka* *Malchus* of *Asiya*, because that is the farthest border of the *Malchus*, its farthest reaches. When He wants to make Himself a bigger King, what does He do? Make His palace bigger? No, He has to push the border out. Where is the border? The border is *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Up to *Malchus* of *Asiya* the *Aibershter* is an uncontested King. When you go past *Malchus* of *Asiya* into the world of the *kelipos*, that is already a no-man's zone: over there the *Malchus* is contested.

blocks.title: Alsace-Lorraine and Kashmir
blocks.text: It is like that place that Germany and France were fighting over ("Alsace-Lorraine"), or like Kashmir, right now, between Pakistan and India: each one says it is theirs. Over here too, the *Malchus* is not accepted.

And how does He become a bigger King? By pushing past the recognized borders of His *Malchus*, which is *Malchus* of *Asiya*, into the world of the *kelipos*. That is what we are trying to do right now: conquer the world for the *Aibershter*. And if we have to conquer the world, why do we have to conquer the world? It means it is not His yet.

blocks.question: What do you mean it is not His? Everything is His: "The earth and its fullness are G-d's."
blocks.text: Yes, but we are talking about a kingdom. The thing of a kingdom is that it has to be recognized.

blocks.title: Iraq: conquered, not consolidated
blocks.text: Over here in this world there is a bunch of rebel bands running around, like they said: didn't Bush conquer Iraq? But in the meantime it is not a full thing yet. ("It hasn't been consolidated." "It hasn't been consolidated, it's not a real *Malchus*." "The sovereignty is not recognized.") Yes, the sovereignty is not recognized; and in sovereignty, especially in *Malchus* as opposed to dictatorship, a *Malchus* is a thing that has to be recognized. The King has to be coronated *davka* by His subjects.

sensitivity.reason: A current-events example naming Bush's conquest of Iraq, which a public edition might read as a political remark.
sensitivity.publishable: Over here in this world there is a bunch of rebel bands running around, as in a country that has been conquered but not yet consolidated: it is not a real *Malchus*, the sovereignty is not recognized. And in sovereignty, especially in *Malchus* as opposed to dictatorship, a *Malchus* is a thing that has to be recognized. The King has to be coronated *davka* by His subjects.

blocks.text: So right now the *Malchus* runs from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* to *Malchus* of *Asiya*: that is the matter of **"I am first and I am last"**, and of "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds," down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

sections.title: Every unification is only a particular: the makif, the primordial thought, and Yachid
sections.summary: The whole joining of beginning and end is one *prat* within the *makif* that circles the *Kav*, the primordial thought; and that in turn is one *prat* before the Essence, which is not even a *klal* to a *prat*. From that *Yachid* the life of all the worlds is drawn.

phrases.he: וכל יחוד וחיבור דראש לסוף זה אחר ההתבוננות בפרטיות רבות שביניהם
phrases.en: And every unification and joining of this beginning to end, after the contemplation of the many particulars between them,

phrases.he: אינו רק כמו פרט אחד לגבי בחינת הכלל הכוללם יחד
phrases.en: is only like one particular compared to the *klal* that includes them all together,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מקיף הכללי דעגול שמקיף לקו
phrases.en: which is the general *makif* of the *igul* (circle) that encompasses the *Kav*.

blocks.text: **And every unification and joining of this beginning to end, after the contemplation of the many particulars between them,** **is only like one particular compared to the *klal* that includes them all together**: the general *makif* of the *igul* (circle) that encompasses the *Kav*, which he reads as the *Kav* of the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought).

blocks.title: One person in Pittsburgh
blocks.text: Any kind of *yichud* that you are making is like that. I am just one person in Pittsburgh; Pittsburgh is just one city in the United States; that is one country in the world; and that whole world, which is what we are going to try to take over, even that is only a *prat* compared to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. And that is only a *prat* compared to *Asiya*, and that only a *prat* compared to the upper *pratim*, all the way until the whole thing is just a *prat* compared to the *machshava kduma*, which includes everything: the general *makif* of the *igul* that encompasses the *Kav*.

phrases.he: וגם הוא פרט אחד יחשב
phrases.en: And it too is counted as one particular

phrases.he: לגבי עצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום שנקרא טהירו עילאה
phrases.en: compared to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, called *tehiru ila'a*,

phrases.he: שלמעלה מהיות גם בחינת כלל לפרט,
phrases.en: which is above being even a *klal* to a *prat*,

phrases.he: מאחר שנקרא קדוש ומובדל בבחינת העצמיות
phrases.en: since it is called holy and separate, in its essence.

blocks.text: **And it too is counted as one particular**: the *machshava kduma* is only one *prat* compared to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, the *tehiru ila'a*. That is **above being even a *klal* to a *prat***: it is not even called a *klal* to a *prat*. It is called holy and separate: it is totally separate from it and has nothing to do with it, in its essence.

phrases.he: וזהו פירוש יחיד חי העולמים
phrases.en: And this is the meaning of "*Yachid* (the Singular), life of the worlds":

phrases.he: מבחינת יחיד זה נמשך על ידי צמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: from this *Yachid* is drawn, through the first *tzimtzum* mentioned above,

phrases.he: להיות נקרא חי כל העולמים דאבי''ע שבקו בבחינת מקיף ופנימי כו'
phrases.en: to be called the life of all the worlds of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* that are in the *Kav*, as *makif* and *pnimi*,

phrases.he: וכידוע ודי למבין.
phrases.en: as is known. This is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **And this is the meaning of "*Yachid* (the Singular), life of the worlds"**: from this *Yachid* is drawn, through the first *tzimtzum*, what is called the life of all the worlds. From *Yachid* comes the *machshava kduma*, and it comes as *makif* and *pnimi*, as is known. "And this will basically be the framework."

sections.title: Training the mind: the short out of the long, down to the physical
sections.summary: Once every particular is learned, a person trains his mind and heart all his life to make the short out of the long, until in one moment, from whatever he sees, he goes whoosh straight to the *Aibershter*. In the physical world itself, seen with physical eyes, the *Ein Sof* rests.

phrases.he: ואחר שיבואר לאדם ביאור כל פרט בסדר השתלשלות זאת,
phrases.en: And after a person has had each particular of this order of *hishtalshelus* explained,

phrases.he: הצריך לכל אדם לידע ולקבוע בנפשו
phrases.en: which every person needs to know and fix in his soul,

phrases.he: הנה תמיד כל ימי חייו ירגיל מוחו ולבו
phrases.en: then always, all the days of his life, he should train his mind and heart,

phrases.he: אחר טוב ידיעתו ורגילותו תמיד בכל פרטיהם דווקא
phrases.en: once he knows it well and is used to it, constantly, in all their particulars, *davka*,

phrases.he: לעשות הקיצור מן האריכות מראש לסוף יחד
phrases.en: to make the short out of the long, from beginning to end together.

blocks.text: After a person has had each particular of this order explained, he must know and fix in his soul that **always, all the days of his life**, the whole time, every day of his life, he should **train his mind and heart** in all their particulars, *davka*, **to make the short out of the long, from beginning to end together**: he should train himself to see immediately that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here.

blocks.question: So why not go like that right away, and just say the Aibershter is here and the Aibershter is here?
blocks.text: That is one of the main complaints against this. The answer is like what the Alter Rebbe answered about the maid. She does not really know that He is here; she just says it. It is just an imagination in her head, and she has no concept of what it is really talking about.

phrases.he: עד שברגע א' ממש בהתבונן בנפשו בסוף הכל,
phrases.en: until, in one moment, *mamash*, when he contemplates in his soul the end of everything,

phrases.he: שהוא השגות איכות התהוות יש מאין הגשם דגלגלים וד' יסודות הגשמיים וכל פרטי עולם הזה השפל
phrases.en: which is the grasp of how the physical comes into being as *yesh* (something) from *ayin* (nothing): the *galgalim* (celestial orbits), the four physical elements and all the details of this lowly world,

blocks.text: **until, in one moment, *mamash***, when he contemplates the end of everything, how the physical comes into being, the *galgalim* (celestial orbits), the four elements and all the details of this world: whenever he sees whatever happened, he can immediately put the whole thing together in one shot, where the *galgalim* go to the *Ofanim* (a class of angels) and through *Asiya*, *Yetzira*, *Beriya*, *Atzilus*. Whoosh, straight to the *Aibershter*, and he says the *Aibershter* did this. There was a hurricane: who did it? It was the *Aibershter*. And the food tasted real good: who did it? It was the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב שאו מרום עיניכם,
phrases.en: as it is written, "Lift up your eyes on high"

phrases.he: בראיה גשמיית,
phrases.en: with physical sight,

phrases.he: וראו מי ברא אלה,
phrases.en: "and see who created these":

phrases.he: בגשמיות התהוותם ליש גמור ממש בצמצום היותר אחרון
phrases.en: in the physicality of their coming into being as a complete *yesh*, *mamash*, in the very last *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שבזה ממש שורה בבחינת אין סוף דוקא
phrases.en: that in this, *mamash*, the *Ein Sof* rests, *davka*,

phrases.he: מבחינת תחלת הכל, שהוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני מקור האצי'
phrases.en: from the beginning of everything, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before the source of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: "**Lift up your eyes on high**," **with physical sight**. And this, by the way, is the *inyan* of *re'iya* (sight): you know that *Moshiach* will bring the thing in a way of *re'iya*. It means that *mamash*, when a person tastes his food, he is tasting the *Aibershter*. "**and see who created these**," in the actual physicality of their coming into being as a complete *yesh*, in the very last *tzimtzum*.

The text says **that in this, *mamash*, the *Ein Sof* rests, *davka***. Now he is bringing in the levels he left out before. Before, he went only down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*; now he brings in the physical. When a person sees the physical in front of him, in that is the *Ein Sof*, *davka*: the beginning of everything, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before *Atzilus*.

sections.title: Why Tehillim praises the bunnies: the middle is transparent
sections.summary: *Tehillim* praises G-d for bunnies and boats and not for angels, because the real thing of the *Aibershter* is *davka* down here. All the levels in between are like a phone line, transparent; and one must want to know the particulars, as a fan or a friend does, because ignoring Someone who is standing right there is the biggest insult.

phrases.he: וע"כ לא נזכר בכל ספר תהלים בשבחי גדולת יהו״ה רק בדרך פשוט,
phrases.en: And therefore the whole Book of *Tehillim* (Psalms) mentions the praises of G-d's greatness only in a simple way:

phrases.he: בגדולות ונפלאות מעשה יהו״ה בשמים וארץ וכל צבאם הגשמיים דוקא
phrases.en: in the great and wondrous works of G-d in heaven and earth and all their physical hosts, *davka*;

phrases.he: ולא נזכר שבחי גדולתו בעולמות העליונים רוחניים
phrases.en: and does not mention the praises of His greatness in the upper, spiritual worlds,

phrases.he: עד רום המעלות שלפני האצילות כו'
phrases.en: up to the highest levels before *Atzilus*.

blocks.question: Bunnies, lions and boats: that is the praise of G-d?
blocks.text: **the whole Book of *Tehillim* (Psalms) mentions the praises of G-d's greatness only in a simple way**. It says that each bunny has a rock to run under, and the young lions roar for their prey, and the boats go on the sea and the waves are so big. So what kind of thing is that? That is the praise of G-d? That is not the praise of G-d. This whole planet is some tiny little nothing. What are you telling me about the bunnies? He says: "No, just the opposite. The whole thing that the *Aibershter* feeds the bunnies and gives each one a rock to hide under, that's the whole thing. That's where you see the actual *Atzmus*."

*Tehillim* **does not mention the praises of His greatness in the upper, spiritual worlds**. It does not talk about the angels and stuff like that. It talks about "Oh, You helped me with my enemy." So what, He helped you with your enemy? Why not talk at least about the angels, and why even about the angels? Talk higher, talk about big things, **up to the highest levels before *Atzilus***. It does not talk about any of those things. Why? Because their beginning is wedged in their end, *davka*: it is down here in the world that the real thing of the *Aibershter* is. As was said before, "I, I am He," *mamash*: I am Him, right here, *davka* with us.

That is because the virtue of the real thing of *Malchus* is to spread out beyond the borders. So when it spreads out beyond the borders down here, past *Malchus* of *Asiya*, there is a spread beyond the borders upstairs too: from *Malchus* after the *tzimtzum* to the *Atzmus* before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: מפני שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן דוקא כנזכר לעיל

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני אני הוא ממש וכו'

phrases.he: ועצמיות אור אין סוף הוא הסובב כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: and the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* is what encompasses [everything]. This is enough for one who understands.

phrases.he: וזהו אמיתית המכוון בהתבוננות בפרט כנזכר לעיל

phrases.he: (וגם שלפי החשבון בפרטי ההשתלשלות, רחוק מאד מאד מראש לסוף,

phrases.en: as it is written, "I, I am He,"

phrases.he: ומבלעדי באמצעיתא כו' ודי למבין)

blocks.text: **by the reckoning of the particulars of the *hishtalshelus* it is very, very far from beginning to end**: it looks very far. But **in truth it is very close, with no break and no hiding at all in the middle**: it is really totally close, with no break at all.

blocks.title: The phone line
blocks.text: All this stuff in the middle is really like nothing. It is like the phone line between us: even though it is a very big phone line, you can totally discount it. We do not think about the phone line. "I'm talking to you like you're *mamash* here," because it is transparent.

So it is with the whole *hishtalshelus*: all the connections in the middle, with all the particulars, this goes into that and that goes into this, but really it is all transparent and totally discounted. As it says, **"I, I am He,"**: it is *mamash* Me, I am right here with you. **"and besides Me" in the middle** there is nothing. I am at the beginning of the thing, I am at the end of the thing, and besides Me there is nothing else: all the middle is not there.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב כי האלהי״ם עשה את האדם
phrases.en: (And as it is written, "For G-d made man"

phrases.he: קדמאה ראשית הקו,
phrases.en: (the first [man], the beginning of the *Kav*)

phrases.he: ישר מראשו לסופו
phrases.en: "straight," from his head to his end,

phrases.he: עד עקב דאדם קדמון שמסתיים בסוף העשיה בבחינת יושר
phrases.en: down to the heel of *Adam Kadmon*, which ends at the end of *Asiya*, as straightness,

phrases.he: שהוא ההתכללות גמור מראשו לסופו,
phrases.en: which is a complete inclusion from his head to his end;

phrases.he: והמה בקשו חשבונות רבים בבחינת העגולים כו'
phrases.en: "but they sought many reckonings," as circles,

phrases.he: בפירוד והתחלקות זה למעלה מזה כו')
phrases.en: in separation and division, one above the other.)

blocks.text: "**For G-d made man**" straight: the *Aibershter* made *Adam Kadmon* totally straight, **from his head to his end**. The business of *Adam Kadmon* is one straight line that goes, poof, straight from there to here, all the way down to the end of *Asiya*, as straightness. That is the way it is, and you have to take it simply: *mamash* the *Aibershter* is here. To the point that you can even forget the *hisbonenus*, like what the Rebbe said, *al daas hatinok hazeh*, according to the mind of this child.

blocks.question: So what do you need all this hisbonenus for? Why all the complications?
blocks.text: Why not do like the simple Jew in all those stories of the Baal Shem Tov, who took a whistle "and stuff like that"? Yes: if you could actually believe, like a baby, that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here, it would be fine. But the problem is that it is not really like that. Why? Because "**they sought many reckonings**," circles, in separation, one above the other. People are not really seeing it straight. You say: if I save my money and put it in an IRA account, then by the time I'm 65... What does anything have to do with that?

Actually, as far as a mitzva goes, you are supposed to do that. You are supposed to go by what the *Rambam* says, live with a budget and stuff like that. But you are not supposed to believe in it. So that is one thing: without the *hisbonenus* you really do not have the actual, real *emuna* (faith) that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here. That is number one.

blocks.title: The fan club
blocks.text: Number two: the sign of a real thing is that you want to know its particulars. You can see this from fan clubs. ("From what?" "Fan clubs.") Like, what's his name, Michael Jackson, or the Beatles: a fan club wants to know everything. You could say, what are you bothering me? I like the music, I'm grooving on it, it's nice music. But for instance, *l'havdil*, Elvis Presley has been dead who knows how many years already, and they still want to know what he did, and this hotel he was in. Who cares? Why? Because if you are a fan, you want to know all the details. If you really believed that the *Aibershter* was here and standing with you, and He is *mamash* your friend, you would want to know all about Him.

blocks.title: Meeting a new guy
blocks.text: You meet a new guy and you want to be friends with him, so you say: "Oh, where you from? And what do you do? Are you married? You got kids?" You want to know all the details. If you do not want to know the details, it means you are really not interested. It is the whole thing of interest: if you show interest in something, you want to know all the details. So if you do not want to know the details, it means you are totally not interested in the *Aibershter*.

You have nothing to do with Him. To you, what does it mean that He is standing here? You say, "Yeah, but I believe He's standing here." "Yeah, but to you it's like He's not there." It is even worse than that: it is an insult. You are ignoring Him. If you do not believe He is there, at least you are not ignoring Him. But if you believe He is there and you are not interested, the guy is standing right there and you will not even say hello to Him; you do not want to talk to Him. He wants to know everything about you, He is interested, and you do not want to know nothing about Him. It is *mamash* an insult, like a guy standing there while you ignore him: the biggest insult you can have.

sections.title: In the Kesarim there is no distance: one will, from the simple will to the will to do
sections.summary: In the *Kesarim* there is no cause and effect with a distance of levels: from the simple will, still *hiyuli*, through the will to emanate and to create, down to the will to make, it is one will, as in a person who wants to walk and walks. A free discussion follows on how this book is to be learned: it is a kindergarten book, and it shows you that you are a worm.

phrases.he: ויובן כל הנזכר לעיל בדרך קצרה מאד בבחינת הכתרים שבכל עולם
phrases.en: All the above can be understood in a very short way from the *Kesarim* (crowns) of each world:

phrases.he: שאין בכתרים בחינת השתלשלות עילה ועלול בריחוק המדרגה כלל
phrases.en: that in the *Kesarim* there is no *hishtalshelus* of cause and effect, with a distance of level, at all.

phrases.he: כמו בחינת הרצון הפשוט שבעצמיות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: Like the simple will in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט כו',
phrases.en: as it says, "When it arose in His simple will":

phrases.he: בחינת מלכות דאין סוף עצמה כשעלה במחשבה הפשוטה אנא אמלוך כו'
phrases.en: *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* itself, when "*Ana Emloch* (I shall rule)" arose in the simple thought,

phrases.he: שהוא למעלה מרצון להאציל או לברוא כו'
phrases.en: which is above a will to emanate or to create,

phrases.he: רק בחינת היולי עדיין
phrases.en: but only *hiyuli* (raw potential) still.

blocks.text: All this can be understood **in a very short way from the *Kesarim* (crowns) of each world**. Really, by the *Kesarim* there is no real spreading out, no cause and effect with a distance of level. It is like the simple will in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*: "when it arose in His simple will," *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* itself, when *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule) arose in the simple thought. That is above a will to emanate or to create: **only *hiyuli* (raw potential) still**.

phrases.he: וממנו נתצמצם תחילה בחינת רצון הקדום שנקרא כתר לאדם קדמון
phrases.en: And from it was first contracted the primordial will, called *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*;

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון להאציל, בחינת כתר דאצילות בכלל
phrases.en: then the will to emanate, *Keser* of *Atzilus* as a whole;

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא, בחינת כתר שבמלכות דבריאה,
phrases.en: then the will to create, *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Beriya*;

phrases.he: ואחר כך כתר מלכות דיצירה כו'
phrases.en: then *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Yetzira*,

phrases.he: עד כתר מלכות דעשיה, הרצון לעשות
phrases.en: down to *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the will to make.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה עשה כו'
phrases.en: As it is written, "All that G-d desired, He did."

blocks.text: From it was first contracted **the primordial will**, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*; then the will to emanate, *Keser* of *Atzilus*; then the will to create, and so on down to *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, **the will to make**. "All that G-d desired, He did": *mamash* like one thing, all one continuum. What He wanted, that is what He did. In a person too, the will to do is not less than the will to think about it. Actually it is more: the whole reason he is thinking about it is because he wants to do it.

phrases.he: ומהו ההפרש באדם התחתון בבחינת רצונו ועצמותו ההיולי
phrases.en: And what difference is there in man below, in his will and his *hiyuli* essence,

phrases.he: שהיה כלול בו ד' רצונות
phrases.en: in which four wills were included,

phrases.he: כמו רצון לעצמות גופו לרצון לפעול ולעשות היותר אחרון,
phrases.en: from the will for the essence of his body to the will to act and do the very last thing?

phrases.he: הכל משרש ומקור אחד יצא כו'
phrases.en: It all came out from one root and source.

phrases.he: כך אין הפרש ממש בין בחינת רצונו הפשוט שנמשך להיות רצון להאציל,
phrases.en: So there is no difference, *mamash*, between His simple will drawn down to be the will to emanate

phrases.he: לבחינת רצונו הפשוט שנמשך להיות חפץ יהו״ה בכל אשר עשה בסוף עולם העשיה שלנו כו' ודי למבין
phrases.en: and His simple will drawn down to be G-d's desire in all that He did at the end of our world of *Asiya*. This is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **And what difference is there in man below**? In his will and his *hiyuli* essence all the wills were included, from the will for the essence of his body to the will to act and do the very last thing: it all comes from one root and source; it is all the same will. **So there is no difference, *mamash***, between His simple will drawn down to be the will to emanate and His simple will drawn down to be G-d's desire in all that He did at the end of our world of *Asiya*. It is *mamash* one thing, all connected, the same as by a person.

blocks.title: Walking without thinking about the nerves
blocks.text: The whole thing is a *mashal* (analogy) so alike that it is the same thing by us. Really, between the mouth and the brain there is a whole bunch of things going on, but when you talk you do not have to think about it. As a matter of fact it is the opposite: when a person walks, if he starts to think about which nerves are going and which muscle to move, he will fall over. He will not be able to walk. The whole thing happens automatically, from the beginning to the end. He wants to walk, he walks. That's it. Poof, he walks.

blocks.title: The widths of lengths
blocks.text: To understand the width (*rochav*) of three lengths (*orech*), it is not enough to understand the three lengths. First you have to understand the widths of two lengths, and there are three of them; only then can you go to the width of three lengths, because it includes not only the three separate lengths but also the three separate widths of two lengths each. With two stones you build two houses: to understand a width of two lengths you have to understand two lengths. With three stones there is already more: length one, length two and length three; the widths of one and two, one and three, two and three; and before you can even go to the three widths together, you have to understand how one-and-two connects to two-and-three, how one-and-two connects to one-and-three, and how one-and-three connects to two-and-three. So it is not six, it is already nine. These are more than combinations, more like permutations: besides how the lengths connect two at a time, you have to understand how the widths of two connect to each other, otherwise you do not have the full width of three.

blocks.text: And that is only up to three. With four it is already a lot more: first each of the four lengths, then the double lengths, then a bunch of triple lengths; and how this double length goes with that double length and this triple length with that triple length; and how a double length goes with another single length, and a triple length with a double length. How does the length of one, two and three connect with three and four? The width gets more and more complicated the more lengths there are to really understand.

blocks.text: And the thing is, it is really all automatic. This is what was discussed about the garments of *or* with an *aleph*, light, and of *or* with an *ayin*, skin: they are both really the same garment. It is not that one is a garment and the other is not. Both are, and not only that: a garment with an *ayin* and a garment with an *aleph* are *mamash* exactly the same garment.

blocks.title: A fifth-grade explanation for a second-grader
blocks.text: What does a garment with an *ayin* mean? It means the explanation is too deep for you, like when you teach a second-grade kid a fifth-grade explanation. Instead of explaining it to him, it makes a big confusion in his head. It is not only that it does not explain it to him: it actually covers up more than before. He ends up more confused than he was before he had the explanation in the first place.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And besides that, they are trying to make *chiddushim* (new insights), to tie together one thing they learned in *Ayin Beis* with another thing they learned in *Torah Or*, with some other thing they learned somewhere else, with a *sicha* (talk) of the Rebbe, and they do not even realize that they might be talking about different things: different lengths, different explanations. Besides that, they really do not even have the length, the *hisbonenus* of the one simple length. Why? Because they started out with fifth grade instead of starting out with kindergarten.

And he may not even have the length, the *hisbonenus* of the one simple length, because he started out with fifth grade instead of with kindergarten.

blocks.text: That is what the key means: what you start with. It is not even first grade yet. The key is not the *aleph-beis*: *Shaarei Orah* is the *aleph-beis*. The key means before the *aleph-beis*, just to know what the basic code is, before you can get into the first principles.

blocks.text: As was already discussed, *Ayin Beis* is very hard to keep in your head all at once: you cannot keep the whole length. The whole thing of a length is that you have to learn all the points of the length and then have the whole length in your head in one shot. A width means you have to learn all the lines and then have all of them together in your head in one shot, to make a surface. A width is not just a width, because if it were just a width it would be a length. A width means with a length: a square, not a line; a surface, a plane. It means you already have the length. There cannot be such a thing as understanding a bunch of points with no length to them: that is not even a length, and if you cannot connect along the length, you cannot connect along the width.

blocks.text: So the basic thing they have and understand is points, points; they do not understand the whole length of it. And even if you try to teach these people a simple explanation from *Shaar HaYichud*, they go and try to relate it to what it says in *Ayin Beis*: they want to do a width. And really they do not understand the length there, and not the length here, and they already want to be on a width. That is basically what is happening.

blocks.text: Because *Shaar HaYichud* is a kindergarten book. It is not even a first-grade book. It is the keys, and keys means openings: before you even go to first grade, just to get you used to learning in the first place, to open it up for you. Like nursery and kindergarten, where you do not yet learn the actual *aleph-beis* with the kids: you just play with them, you let them paint an *aleph*, and they sing songs and stuff like that. Just openings. So if a person could actually understand the length of *Ayin Beis*, he would certainly be able to understand a kindergarten book like this.

You will make dark from the light and light from the dark, and you will end up doing like Shabsai Tzvi and becoming a Muslim, G-d forbid. Or even if you stay a Jew, you will mix it all up in your head, and you will have a Judaism that is really *avoda zara* (idolatry), "which most people do have."

blocks.title: The grandson who found an aleph
blocks.text: It is like Rabbi Markel's grandson. Now he is a little more advanced, but when he was two or three he started catching on to letters. Rabbi Markel would be sitting there reading a book, it could be a very complicated book like *Shaar HaYichud* or *Ayin Beis*, or a *Chumash*, or whatever, and the boy would look and say, "Oh, look, an *aleph*!" He knows the *aleph* just like his grandfather knows the *aleph*. And that is the whole thing: they understand this tiny little *aleph*. Never mind that they do not understand the *inyan*: they do not understand the sentence, not even a word. They understand a letter, and that is all they understand. What they understand there is the same as Shuli understanding that this is an *aleph*. "Oh, here's another *aleph*!" But to his grandfather these are two different *alephs*, because this is an *aleph* in one word and that is an *aleph* in another word. Not only that: this other word is part of a whole other *inyan*. So it is a whole different *aleph*.

They will tell you about a *helem* (concealment) that is in existence and a *helem* that is not in existence, and *hispashtus min ha'etzem* (spreading forth from the essence); but this is just a letter. They have no idea how it fits into anything. It is all confusion in their head. Over there they do not see it; over here it is such a small book that you can see that it is all confusion in your head.

blocks.text: Just from the fact that he says a *helem* that is in existence and a *helem* that is not, and continues talking about the *inyan*, you can see that you do not really understand what it has to do with what he is talking about. Over there it is five chapters; it could be five chapters just on the *helem* that is not in existence, so you think you understand: "I understood five whole chapters over there." But those five chapters are really part of fifty chapters on some *inyan*, and even the fifty chapters are only a *prat*. ("Yeah, the fifty chapters is a word.") This is a letter, and the fifty chapters are a word: you did not even get to a sentence yet. It is like understanding just a word without understanding anything, like if I tell you "the". "The" what?

blocks.title: Any book will do
blocks.text: So the basic thing over there is that their understanding is all points, points, and that is *mamash* the same thing as Shuli. For Shuli it does not matter where you open up the book: he will look and say, "There's an *aleph*, look!" Anywhere he opens up the book he can find little things that he knows, and he gets a big pleasure out of it: "Oh, *beis*!" "Oh, look, an *ayin*!" It does not matter where you open up the book, and it does not matter which book you open up. You can open up *Imrei Bina*, he understands just as well. You can open up *Yedios Achronos*, the same thing for him: here is an *aleph* and here is a *beis*.

Basically, when you open up this book, you realize that you are not a human being. You do not even know how to think properly. Till you learn this book you have no *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought). Basically what it tells you is: never mind that you are a kindergarten kid, you are a beast. And when you start learning it a little bit you say, "Wait a minute, it's not even a beast."

blocks.title: A worm on your hand
blocks.text: This is what David HaMelech says: "I am a worm and not a man." My relationship to what it really says here is not even a beast's. A beast, a dog and a sheep, has some understanding of humans. A dog does not *mamash* understand what humans are, he cannot go to college or something, but he can relate to humans: he knows that if you give a big smile and wag your tail, they will give you a cookie. So there is some kind of relationship. A cat, a dog, a sheep can relate to humans, even though it is still a beast. A worm has no relationship to a human. Even if you put him on your hand and he is crawling around, he does not even know he is crawling around on your hand. He is not even scared, like a squirrel is scared. He is totally oblivious; he does not know what is going on at all. That is what David HaMelech says: I am a worm and not a person. And this is basically what happens here: it tells you that you are a worm.

blocks.text: This is what was discussed yesterday, the inwardness of the Essence. In order to learn *Chassidus*, as he said "at the end of chapter... what was it, six," you have to have *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice). *Mesirus nefesh* means to give up your *ratzon* (will); *nefesh* means *ratzon*, as you can read in some places. You have to give up your *ratzon*, because your *ratzon* is basically to be a big shot.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the chapter give a general overview before the particulars, and what does the chain show about the *sefiros*?
What is the whole purpose of contemplating all the particulars, and what does the conference call have to do with it?
Which two levels does the order of *hishtalshelus* leave out, and where are they brought back in?
Why is *Malchus* of *Asiya* the biggest *Malchus*, and how does the King become a bigger King?
Why does *Tehillim* praise G-d for the bunnies and not for the angels?
If the *Aibershter* is simply here, what is all the *hisbonenus* for? Give both reasons.

notes.text: Class 053 w18-59: he lists the earlier introductions as "the hakdamos of the chedva and dechiya, and the yesh and the ayin"; the first pair is not clear and is left out of the block.

Line 28 prints "והנה אחר, היחוד"; he reads it as "והנה אך היחוד" (053 w1924-1933, partly garbled) and renders it "Only when you look good... then" (w1948). The phrases follow his reading: the printed אחר is taken as אך, "But the unification:", with "only" carried into line 29.

In class 053 he reads slightly different words in several lines: ייגע for ירגיל (line 42), כוונת for קוטב (line 12), דמחשבה סתימאה added to line 19 and דמחשבה קדומה to line 36, "בדרך שאר המאמרים" for "בדרך קצרה מאד" in line 55 (class 054), and "כל הרצונות" for "ד' רצונות" in line 63. The phrases follow the printed text.

Class 053 w3787 ("מפני שנושא תהלתך בסופם") is his reading of the opening of line 49 ("מפני שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן דוקא") at the end of the tape, misheard by the transcript; the block renders it from the line. It stays under lines 47-48, which it explains, and class 054 reads line 49 again.
"And va'ed is echad" (053 w2212-2216) is said without explanation; kept as said.

He reads the verse in line 53 as "the Aibershter made Adam Kadmon straight" (Koheles 7:29, "G-d made man straight, but they sought many reckonings"); the phrases put "straight" where the verse has it.

Class 055 reads no line. It is a free discussion on how the book is to be learned: lengths and widths of understanding and the garments of or with an aleph and an ayin, both picked up from an earlier class ("what we were talking about yesterday"), and mesirus nefesh "at the end of chapter six", though NOTES.md says chapters 5-6 were recorded after 7-9. All its blocks are under the chapter's last passage, with outOfPlace. Its first words start mid-sentence: the tape begins in the middle of the discussion.

"The key" and "keys means openings" (055 w825-1299): he seems to refer to a title or description of Shaar HaYichud as keys (mafteichos); he does not say whose. Yedios Achronos is an Israeli daily newspaper; Imrei Bina is a work of the Mitteler Rebbe.
The Alter Rebbe and the maid (053 w3291-3333) is only alluded to; chapter 3 or 4 of this series tells it in full. The block keeps his short form.
"Like what the Rebbe said, al daas hatinok hazeh" (054 w430-439): he does not say where; kept as said.
